speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you're experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand what's happening, has the knee swelling been accompanied by redness or warmth?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

Given your history of a self-resolving joint issue, current knee inflammation, and urinary symptoms, combined with your sexual history, this strongly suggests a post-infectious autoimmune reaction. We need to confirm the infection and inflammation markers; can you tell me if you have any eye irritation, such as redness or blurred vision? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
